text.en: Saba and Aparna sit in the school garden looking at their seasons' journal of what they noticed through the year.

All year you have been curious explorers observing plants, animals, sunlight, water and human activities. Now bring it together.
Step 1: make a large wall chart. The columns are April to June, July to September, October to December and January to March. The rows are plant life, birds and animals, air, heat and light, water and water bodies, and human activities.
Step 2: write your journal observations on the chart so everyone can see the whole picture.
Step 3: form five groups, one for each theme. Make a poster on how your theme changed through the year. For example, plant life shows leaves, flowers and fruits in different months, and water shows ponds, puddles and rain.
Step 4: form four new groups, one per time period, with a member from each theme. Study all five themes for that time period and write a short story linking nature and people's lives, such as January to March.
Compare notes: do the same things happen every year? They follow a natural rhythm.
Keep observing and journaling so you notice patterns, such as signs of coming rain.
(additional, not in the textbook) Be careful and gentle when observing animals and plants; do not disturb them.

problem.en: How do we find patterns in a year?

text.en: Note observations every month.
Put them on a chart by time and theme.
Compare across the year.

prompt.en: How did you track change in nature through the year?

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking you can see patterns in one day

points.en: A chart shows patterns by month and theme.
